stem: A researcher in Colombo, Sri Lanka, selected 1,000 adults at random from the city's adult residents. Adults who owned a bicycle reported more hours of outdoor activity per week, on average, than adults who did not. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

choices.A: Among adults in Colombo, owning a bicycle is associated with more hours of outdoor activity per week.
choices.B: The result applies only to the 1,000 adults in the sample.
choices.C: Owning a bicycle causes adults in Colombo to spend more hours on outdoor activity per week.
choices.D: Spending more hours outdoors causes adults in Colombo to buy bicycles.

solution: The adults were selected at random from the city, so the result can be generalized to adults in Colombo.
No one was assigned to own a bicycle, so the study shows an association, not cause and effect.

explanation.A: Correct. A random sample supports generalizing the association to all adults in Colombo.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Because the sample was random, the result can be generalized beyond the 1,000 adults.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without random assignment, other factors could explain the difference, so a causal claim is not supported.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is also a cause-and-effect claim, just in the opposite direction; an observational study supports neither.
